#### Mock exam: Building Contracts Mock Exam

*24 questions · 20 minutes · pass mark 70%.* Ten questions drawn from the level's bank, from interfaces and inheritance to tokens, the ABI, gas, testing and deployment.

**Question 1** · One answer · `sol-medium-01`

`Booth.sell` reverts with the custom error `SoldOut(uint256 left, uint256 wanted)` when too
many tickets are asked for. The booth has 2 tickets left, and a test calls
`agent.onlyStrings(booth, 5)`:

```solidity
contract Agent {
    function onlyStrings(IBooth booth, uint256 tickets) external returns (bool) {
        try booth.sell(tickets) returns (uint256) {
            return true;
        } catch Error(string memory) {
            return false;
        }
    }
}
```

What happens?

- **✔ A. The call reverts with `SoldOut(2, 5)`: no catch clause matches a custom error, so the `try` statement passes the error on**
- B. It returns `false`, because `catch Error(string memory)` catches every revert of the called contract
- C. It returns `false` and the booth keeps the 5 tickets sold, because a caught call keeps its changes
- D. It does not compile: `try` needs a `catch Panic(uint256)` clause as well

> **Why:** `catch Error(string memory reason)` only matches errors raised with `revert("...")` or
> `require(cond, "...")`. A custom error is encoded with its own selector, so it matches no
> clause here, and when nothing matches, the whole `try` statement reverts with the callee's
> data: forge reports `[FAIL: SoldOut(2, 5)]`. Add `catch (bytes memory data)` (custom errors
> and empty reverts) or a bare `catch { ... }` to handle every failure. Even when a clause does
> catch, the callee's changes are undone; a catch block never keeps a half-finished call. Any
> subset of clauses is allowed, so the code compiles.

**Question 2** · True or false · `sol-medium-02`

Alice calls `open{value: 0.25 ether}(bob)` on this factory:

```solidity
contract Escrow {
    address public immutable buyer;
    address public immutable seller;

    constructor(address seller_) payable {
        buyer = msg.sender;
        seller = seller_;
    }
}

contract EscrowFactory {
    function open(address seller) external payable returns (Escrow) {
        return new Escrow{value: msg.value}(seller);
    }
}
```

True or false: the new escrow records Alice as its `buyer`.

- A. True
- **✔ B. False**

> **Why:** False. `new` is a call from the factory, so inside `Escrow`'s constructor `msg.sender` is
> the `EscrowFactory`, not Alice; a test that logs both addresses shows the buyer equal to the
> factory. The ether does arrive (the constructor is `payable` and `{value: ...}` forwards it),
> which makes the bug easy to miss. Pass the user in explicitly:
> `new Escrow{value: msg.value}(msg.sender, seller)` with a constructor that stores its
> arguments. The same care applies to any address you are handed: converting it to a contract
> type checks nothing, so a contract only trusts addresses it created or verified.

**Question 3** · One answer · `sol-medium-03`

```solidity
contract Base {
    function trail() public pure virtual returns (string memory) {
        return "Base";
    }
}

contract Audited is Base {
    function trail() public pure virtual override returns (string memory) {
        return string.concat("Audited > ", super.trail());
    }
}

contract Metered is Base {
    function trail() public pure virtual override returns (string memory) {
        return string.concat("Metered > ", super.trail());
    }
}

contract Final is Audited, Metered {
    function trail() public pure override(Audited, Metered) returns (string memory) {
        return string.concat("Final > ", super.trail());
    }
}
```

What does `new Final().trail()` return?

- **✔ A. `Final > Metered > Audited > Base`**
- B. `Final > Audited > Metered > Base`
- C. `Final > Metered > Base`
- D. `Final > Audited > Base > Metered > Base`

> **Why:** Solidity lists bases from "most base-like" to "most derived", so in `is Audited, Metered`
> the last one, `Metered`, is closest to `Final`. C3 linearization gives the line `Final,
> Metered, Audited, Base`, and every `super` call moves one step along it. So `super` inside
> `Metered` calls `Audited`, a contract `Metered` knows nothing about, and `Base` runs once,
> at the end. Python's order is the reverse, which is where `Final > Audited > Metered` comes
> from. Swapping the bases to `is Metered, Audited` gives `Audited` before `Metered`.

**Question 4** · One answer · `sol-medium-04`

`contract Audited is Base` is declared as usual. What does solc 0.8.38 say about this line?

```solidity
contract Wrong is Audited, Base {}
```

- **✔ A. `Error (5005): Linearization of inheritance graph impossible`**
- B. Nothing: listing `Base` again is redundant but allowed in any position
- C. `Error (9097): Identifier already declared.`, because `Base` is inherited twice
- D. `Error (3656): Contract "Wrong" should be marked as abstract.`

> **Why:** Bases go from most base-like to most derived. Writing `Audited, Base` asks for `Base` to
> come after (closer to `Wrong` than) `Audited`, but `Audited` already says it comes after
> `Base`. That contradiction cannot be linearized, so solc stops with error 5005. Write
> `contract Wrong is Base, Audited {}` or, simpler, `contract Wrong is Audited {}`, since
> `Audited` brings `Base` along. Inheriting the same base through two paths is normal (it
> appears once in the line), and nothing here is left unimplemented.

**Question 5** · One answer · `sol-medium-05`

```solidity
library Tally {
    function add(mapping(address => uint256) storage totals, address who, uint256 amount) external returns (uint256) {
        totals[who] += amount;
        return totals[who];
    }
}

contract Scoreboard {
    mapping(address => uint256) public points;

    function score(uint256 amount) external returns (uint256) {
        return Tally.add(points, msg.sender, amount);
    }
}
```

`add` is `external`, so `Tally` is deployed as its own contract. When `Scoreboard.score(3)`
runs, where does the 3 get stored?

- **✔ A. In `Scoreboard`'s storage: the library runs by DELEGATECALL in the scoreboard's context and receives the mapping as its slot number**
- B. In `Tally`'s storage, since the code runs in the library's own contract
- C. Nowhere: the mapping is copied into memory for the call, so the change is lost
- D. The call reverts: a library cannot write to storage

> **Why:** A `public` or `external` library function is called with DELEGATECALL: the library's code
> runs with the caller's storage, `msg.sender` and balance. A `storage` parameter is passed as
> a reference (its slot, here 0), so `totals[who] += amount` writes `Scoreboard`'s `points`.
> Libraries cannot have state variables of their own, and mappings can never be copied to
> memory. Internal library functions skip all of this: their code is compiled into the caller.

**Question 6** · Select all that apply · `sol-medium-06`

A file declares `type Grams is uint256;` and nothing else for it yet. Which statements are
true? Choose all that apply.

- **✔ A. `Grams` values are encoded in the ABI exactly like `uint256`**
- **✔ B. To make `a + b` work, the same file needs `using {add as +} for Grams global;` with a `pure` function `add(Grams, Grams) returns (Grams)`**
- C. `a == b` already compiles, because every type supports equality
- D. A `Grams` can be passed where a `uint256` parameter is expected, since the underlying type is the same

> **Why:** A user-defined value type keeps its underlying type's representation and ABI, but it has no
> operators at all, not even `==`, and no implicit conversions: use `Grams.wrap(x)` and
> `Grams.unwrap(g)`. Operators come from `pure` free (or library) functions attached in a
> `global` using-for directive, which is allowed only in the file that declares the type;
> without `global`, solc says `Operators can only be defined in a global 'using for'
> directive.` That strictness is the point: `weight * price` with two different types becomes
> a compile error instead of a silent bug.

**Question 7** · One answer · `sol-medium-07`

Alice has approved Bob to spend 100 of her tokens. She sends `approve(bob, 50)` to lower the
allowance. Bob watches pending transactions and gets his own transaction included before
hers. With a standard ERC-20, what is the most Bob can end up taking?

- **✔ A. 150: he spends the old 100 first, then the new 50 once Alice's approval lands**
- B. 50: `approve` sets the allowance, so only the newest value ever counts
- C. 100: an allowance can be spent only once, whatever it is later set to
- D. 0: a pending `approve` freezes the allowance until it is included

> **Why:** `approve` **replaces** the allowance; it does not know what was already spent. Bob's
> `transferFrom` of 100 runs first under the old allowance, then Alice's transaction sets a
> fresh allowance of 50, which he also spends. A Foundry test that replays that order logs
> `Bob took 150 coupons`. EIP-20 asks clients to set an allowance to 0 before setting a new
> value, and good habits are approving exact amounts and avoiding unlimited approvals. The
> token contract itself should not enforce the reset, for compatibility.

**Question 8** · Select all that apply · `sol-medium-08`

Which statements about OpenZeppelin Contracts 5.7's `ERC20` are true? Choose all that apply.

- **✔ A. To add a rule to every transfer, mint and burn, you override `_update` and call `super._update(from, to, value)`**
- **✔ B. A contract that inherits `ERC20` and `ERC20Capped` and overrides `_update` must write `override(ERC20, ERC20Capped)`**
- C. You customise transfers by overriding `_beforeTokenTransfer`, which every mint and burn calls
- D. `transferFrom` lowers an allowance of `type(uint256).max` like any other and emits `Approval`

> **Why:** Version 5 replaced the `_beforeTokenTransfer`/`_afterTokenTransfer` hooks with one internal
> virtual function, `_update`, which `_mint` (`from` is zero), `_burn` (`to` is zero) and
> `_transfer` all call; those three are not virtual. Forget `super._update` and nothing moves:
> a test minting 100 tokens then reads a balance and a supply of 0. Because `ERC20Capped` also
> defines `_update`, a bare `override` fails with `Function needs to specify overridden
> contracts "ERC20" and "ERC20Capped".` Finally, `_spendAllowance` never lowers an unlimited
> allowance, and `transferFrom` does not emit `Approval` in 5.x.

**Question 9** · One answer · `sol-medium-09`

A free badge is limited to one per address. A contract calls `claim()`, and its
`onERC721Received` calls `badge.claim()` again whenever it holds fewer than 5 badges, then
returns the magic value:

```solidity
contract OpenDayBadge is ERC721 {
    mapping(address => bool) public claimed;
    uint256 public nextId = 1;

    error AlreadyClaimed(address who);

    constructor() ERC721("Open Day", "OPEN") {}

    function claim() external {
        if (claimed[msg.sender]) revert AlreadyClaimed(msg.sender);
        _safeMint(msg.sender, nextId++);
        claimed[msg.sender] = true;
    }
}
```

How many badges does the contract hold when its first `claim()` returns?

- **✔ A. 5: every nested `claim` runs inside `_safeMint`, before `claimed` is set, so the check passes each time**
- B. 1: the second `claim` reverts with `AlreadyClaimed`, because the first one has already minted
- C. None: `_safeMint` reverts with `ERC721InvalidReceiver` because the receiver calls back into the token
- D. 1: OpenZeppelin's `ERC721` blocks reentrant calls during `_safeMint`

> **Why:** `_safeMint` mints and then calls `onERC721Received` on a contract receiver, so the receiver's
> code runs in the middle of `claim`, before `claimed[msg.sender] = true`. Each nested `claim`
> finds the flag still false and mints again; a test of exactly this contract logged
> `badges held by one address: 5`. OpenZeppelin's `ERC721` has no reentrancy guard, and the
> receiver returned the magic value, so nothing is rejected. The fix is
> checks-effects-interactions: set `claimed` before `_safeMint`. Then the nested call reverts
> with `AlreadyClaimed`, and that revert undoes the whole attempt.

**Question 10** · Select all that apply · `sol-medium-10`

Which statements about an OpenZeppelin 5.x `ERC721` token are true? Choose all that apply.

- **✔ A. After any transfer, `getApproved(id)` returns the zero address**
- **✔ B. An operator set with `setApprovalForAll(operator, true)` may move every token the owner holds in that contract, including ones the owner receives later**
- C. `safeTransferFrom` to an externally owned account calls its `onERC721Received` and reverts if there is no answer
- D. `_mint` to a contract without `onERC721Received` reverts with `ERC721InvalidReceiver`

> **Why:** Every transfer clears the token's approved address (a test printed
> `approval after transfer: 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000`), so a new owner never
> inherits someone else's approval. Operator approval covers the whole collection, now and
> later, which is why phishing sites ask for it. The receiver hook is called only when the
> recipient has code; an account without code is never called. `_mint` does not call the hook
> at all: it happily sends a token to a contract that can never move it, which is why
> OpenZeppelin discourages it in favour of `_safeMint`, which reverts with
> `ERC721InvalidReceiver` in that case.

**Question 11** · One answer · `sol-medium-11`

`0xDEAD` is an address with no code. What does this line give in a Foundry test?

```solidity
(bool ok, bytes memory data) = address(0xDEAD).call(abi.encodeCall(Counter.add, (3)));
```

- **✔ A. `ok` is `true` and `data` is empty: the EVM treats a call to an address without code as a success**
- B. `ok` is `false` and `data` is empty, because there is no function to run
- C. The line reverts, because Solidity checks that the target has code before every call
- D. `ok` is `false` and `data` holds the error `FunctionNotFound()`

> **Why:** A low-level `call` to an address without code succeeds and returns nothing; the test printed
> `no code: true 0`. Solidity adds a code check only to calls through a contract type or an
> interface, and those revert on an empty address. The low-level members `call`,
> `staticcall` and `delegatecall` skip it, so a relay must check `target.code.length`
> itself, or a payment or command can "succeed" without doing anything. There is no built-in
> `FunctionNotFound` error: a contract without a matching function and without a fallback
> reverts with empty data.

**Question 12** · One answer · `sol-medium-12`

A raffle gives each entrant a ticket id `keccak256(abi.encodePacked(name, town))`, where
`name` and `town` are strings the entrants choose. Two different entrants turn out to get the
same id. Which change fixes this?

- **✔ A. Hash `abi.encode(name, town)` instead**
- B. Hash with `sha256` instead of `keccak256`
- C. Put a separator between them: `abi.encodePacked(name, "|", town)`
- D. Swap the arguments: `abi.encodePacked(town, name)`

> **Why:** `abi.encodePacked` joins the bytes without lengths, so `("Ann", "abel")` and
> `("Anna", "bel")` both become `Annabel` and hash the same (a test printed
> `Annabel Annabel` and `true`). Any hash function of the same bytes collides the same way,
> and swapping the order only moves the problem. A separator helps until someone puts the
> separator in a name. `abi.encode` stores each string's offset and length, so different pairs
> give different bytes: `keccak256(abi.encode("ab", "c")) == keccak256(abi.encode("a", "bc"))`
> is false. Use packed mode only when at most one value is dynamic.

**Question 13** · One answer · `sol-medium-13`

A storage slot holds `5`. In a new transaction, a function writes `7` to it; nothing has
touched the slot earlier in the transaction. On the `osaka` EVM, about how much gas does
the write itself cost?

- **✔ A. 5,000: 2,900 for changing a non-zero value plus 2,100 because the slot is cold**
- B. 22,100, because every write to storage costs the same as creating the slot
- C. 2,900, because cold access is only charged for reads
- D. 100, because the slot already holds a value

> **Why:** Changing a non-zero value to another non-zero value costs 2,900, and the first access to a
> slot in a transaction adds the cold surcharge of 2,100 (EIP-2929), for 5,000 in all; measured
> with `gasleft()` around the line it came to 5,020, the extra 20 being the measuring itself.
> 22,100 is the price of turning a zero into a non-zero value, the most expensive write. The
> cold surcharge applies to writes as well as reads. 100 is what a write costs once the slot
> is warm and has already been written in the same transaction.

**Question 14** · Select all that apply · `sol-medium-14`

Which statements about gas on the sandbox's EVM are true? Choose all that apply.

- **✔ A. Setting a non-zero slot to zero earns a refund of 4,800, and refunds cannot exceed a fifth of the transaction's gas**
- **✔ B. A call can pass on at most 63/64 of the gas the caller has left**
- C. Memory costs a fixed 3 gas per word, so allocating ten times the words costs ten times the gas
- D. `vm.lastFrameGas().gasTotalUsed` already has the refund subtracted

> **Why:** EIP-3529 set the clearing refund to 4,800 and capped refunds at one fifth of the gas used.
> EIP-150's 63/64 rule leaves the caller enough gas to handle a failing callee: a caller with
> 999,536 gas left handed a callee 981,163. Memory adds a quadratic term to its 3 gas per word,
> so allocating 10,000 words cost 256,282 gas against 8,712 for 1,000. `gasTotalUsed` is
> counted before refunds, and `gasRefunded` is reported beside it: clearing a slot showed
> `26606` used and `4800` refunded.

**Question 15** · One answer · `sol-medium-15`

A sign-up sheet allows one change per address per day:

```solidity
function book(uint256 n) external {
    uint256 last = lastChange[msg.sender];
    if (block.timestamp < last + 1 days) revert TooSoon(last + 1 days);
    lastChange[msg.sender] = block.timestamp;
    seats[msg.sender] = n;
}
```

A Foundry test deploys the sheet and calls `book(2)` straight away, without any `vm.warp`.
What happens?

- **✔ A. It reverts with `TooSoon(86400)`: the test chain starts at timestamp 1, and an address that never booked has `last == 0`**
- B. It books 2 seats: a first booking can never be too soon
- C. It reverts with `panic: arithmetic underflow or overflow (0x11)`
- D. It reverts with `TooSoon(86401)`, one day after the current timestamp

> **Why:** A mapping returns 0 for an address that never booked, so the check compares the current
> timestamp, 1 on a fresh test chain, with `0 + 1 days`, and refuses: the run failed with
> `TooSoon(86400 [8.64e4])`. On mainnet the clock is far past one day, so the same code lets
> the first booking through: tests and production disagree. Treat a zero timestamp as
> "never" (`last != 0 && ...`). Nothing is subtracted, so there is no underflow, and the error
> reports `last + 1 days`, not the current time plus a day.

**Question 16** · One answer · `sol-medium-16`

Which of these is a sound use of block data?

- **✔ A. Closing a sale when `block.timestamp >= closesAt`, with `closesAt` set days ahead**
- B. Picking a raffle winner from `keccak256(abi.encode(block.prevrandao, block.timestamp))`
- C. A one-day cooldown written as `block.number >= lastBlock + 7200` on any chain
- D. Seeding a game with `blockhash(block.number)`, the hash of the current block

> **Why:** Timestamps are fine for deadlines measured in minutes, hours or days: on Ethereum a block's
> timestamp is fixed by its 12-second slot, and other chains keep it within known bounds.
> Anything computed from block data in a transaction can be computed by another contract in
> the same transaction, and the proposer knows `prevrandao` in advance, so a raffle seeded that
> way can be gamed. 7,200 blocks is a day only at exactly 12 seconds a block; block times
> differ between chains, and empty slots stretch them. `blockhash(block.number)` is always
> zero, because the current block has no hash yet.

**Question 17** · One answer · `sol-medium-17`

In `RoomBooking`, a day that is already booked makes `book` revert with
`AlreadyBooked(day)`. Alice has booked day 20000. This test checks that Bob cannot book it
too. Bob has never been given any ether.

```solidity
function test_RevertWhen_DayTaken() public {
    hoax(alice, 1 ether);
    room.book{value: 0.05 ether}(DAY);
    vm.prank(bob);
    vm.expectRevert();
    room.book{value: 0.05 ether}(DAY);
}
```

What does `forge test` report, and what does that tell you?

- **✔ A. `[PASS]`, but for the wrong reason: the call fails with `EvmError: OutOfFunds` because Bob has no ether, and a bare `expectRevert()` accepts any failure, so the test would pass even without the `AlreadyBooked` check**
- B. `[PASS]`, and it proves the `AlreadyBooked` check works, because the call reverted after `vm.prank(bob)`
- C. `[FAIL]`, because `vm.expectRevert()` without arguments expects a revert string and gets a custom error
- D. `[FAIL]`, because Bob has no ether, so `vm.prank` refuses to make him the caller

> **Why:** A bare `vm.expectRevert()` passes for **any** revert. Here the call never even reaches
> `book`: sending 0.05 ether from an account with nothing fails first with `OutOfFunds`. So
> the test passes, and it would still pass if someone deleted the `AlreadyBooked` check. With
> the exact expectation, `vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(RoomBooking.AlreadyBooked.selector, DAY))`,
> the same test fails with `Error != expected error: EvmError: OutOfFunds != AlreadyBooked(20000 [2e4])`,
> which reveals the missing `hoax(bob, 1 ether)`. Fund every actor and expect the exact error.
> `vm.prank` works for any address, funded or not.

**Question 18** · Select all that apply · `sol-medium-18`

Which statements about Foundry 1.8 tests are true? Choose all that apply.

- **✔ A. In `vm.prank(alice); room.book{value: room.DEPOSIT()}(DAY);` the prank is used up by the `DEPOSIT()` call, so `book` is called by the test contract**
- **✔ B. `hoax(alice, 1 ether)` gives Alice 1 ether and makes her the caller of the next call**
- **✔ C. After `vm.mockCall(registry, abi.encodeWithSelector(IMembership.isMember.selector), abi.encode(true))`, a second mock with the full calldata `abi.encodeCall(IMembership.isMember, (bob))` decides the answer for Bob**
- D. A test named `testFail_Cancel` passes when its body reverts, so it is the usual way to test reverts

> **Why:** A prank applies to the very next call, and an argument such as `room.DEPOSIT()` is
> evaluated, as a call, before `book`; the test then fails with `who booked the day:
> 0x7FA9...1496 != 0x3288...dac6`. Read such values into a local variable before the prank.
> `hoax` from forge-std is `deal` plus `prank`. For `mockCall`, a full calldata match is
> looked up before a selector-only (prefix) match, so the specific mock wins for Bob while the
> general one still answers for everyone else. `testFail` tests are gone from Foundry 1.x:
> forge fails such a test with a message saying that `testFail*` has been removed and
> suggesting a `test_Revert[If|When]_Condition` test that expects the revert.

**Question 19** · One answer · `sol-medium-19`

In this escrow the stages are `AwaitingPayment` (0), `Paid` (1), `Expired` (2), `Released`
(3) and `Refunded` (4). `timedTransitions` moves `Paid` to `Expired` once
`block.timestamp > confirmBy`. A developer writes the modifiers in this order:

```solidity
function claimRefund() external onlyBuyer atStage(Stage.Expired) timedTransitions {
    _moveTo(Stage.Refunded);
    owed[buyer] += price;
}
```

The buyer paid, and calls `claimRefund()` one day after the deadline. What happens?

- **✔ A. It reverts with `WrongStage(2, 1)`: `atStage` runs first and still sees `Paid`, so the refund can never be claimed**
- B. It succeeds: all modifiers run before the body, so their order does not matter
- C. It reverts with `WrongStage(1, 2)`, because `timedTransitions` has already moved the stage to `Expired`
- D. It succeeds the second time it is called, because the first call stored `Expired` before reverting

> **Why:** Modifiers run from left to right, each wrapping the rest. `atStage(Stage.Expired)` checks
> the stored stage, which is still `Paid`, and reverts with `WrongStage(expected 2, actual 1)`
> before `timedTransitions` can apply the deadline. Nothing is stored by a reverted call, so
> every later attempt fails the same way and the buyer's money is stuck. Put
> `timedTransitions` before `atStage`. Even in the right order, a transition made inside a call
> that then reverts is undone with it.

**Question 20** · One answer · `sol-medium-20`

A prize contract holds 3 ether and pays three winners in one function:

```solidity
function payOut() external {
    uint256 share = address(this).balance / winners.length;
    for (uint256 i = 0; i < winners.length; i++) {
        (bool ok,) = winners[i].call{value: share}("");
        if (!ok) revert TransferFailed(winners[i]);
    }
}
```

The second winner is a contract whose `receive` function reverts. What happens, and what is
the standard fix?

- **✔ A. `payOut` reverts with `TransferFailed(<second winner>)` every time, so nobody is paid; credit each winner's share in a mapping and let each one withdraw it**
- B. The first winner is paid and the other two are not; add `nonReentrant` to `payOut`
- C. The first and third winners are paid and the second share stays in the contract; nothing needs fixing
- D. It runs out of gas because of the loop; send with `transfer` instead of `call`

> **Why:** A revert undoes the whole call, including the payment already made to the first winner, so
> one refusing recipient blocks everyone, now and on every retry: the test shows
> `[FAIL: TransferFailed(0x5615dEB798BB3E4dFa0139dFa1b3D433Cc23b72f)]`. Ignoring `ok` instead
> would hide the failure and leave money behind silently. The **withdrawal (pull) pattern**
> records `owed[winner] += share` and lets each winner call `withdraw`, so a refuser only
> fails its own withdrawal. Reentrancy is not the problem here, and `transfer` is deprecated
> and would revert just the same.

**Question 21** · One answer · `sol-medium-21`

```solidity
constructor(IERC20 token_, address admin) {
    token = token_;
    _grantRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, admin);
    _setRoleAdmin(GUARDIAN_ROLE, GRANTER_ROLE);
}
```

The admin has granted `GRANTER_ROLE` to Gina. Now the admin calls
`grantRole(GUARDIAN_ROLE, admin)` on this OpenZeppelin 5.x `AccessControl` contract. What
happens?

- **✔ A. It reverts with `AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount(admin, GRANTER_ROLE)`: only holders of a role's admin role may grant it**
- B. It succeeds, because `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` may grant every role
- C. It reverts with `AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount(admin, GUARDIAN_ROLE)`
- D. It reverts with `OwnableUnauthorizedAccount(admin)`

> **Why:** `grantRole(role, account)` is guarded by `onlyRole(getRoleAdmin(role))`. `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`
> is every role's admin only until `_setRoleAdmin` changes it; here the admin of
> `GUARDIAN_ROLE` is `GRANTER_ROLE`, which the admin does not hold. The error names the
> caller and the **missing** role, `keccak256("GRANTER_ROLE")`, as in the real run:
> `AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount(0xaA10...9ecF, 0x2dee5dd8...ed6a)`. Gina, a granter, can
> appoint guardians. `AccessControl` has nothing to do with `Ownable`'s errors.

**Question 22** · Select all that apply · `sol-medium-22`

Which statements about OpenZeppelin Contracts 5.x are true? Choose all that apply.

- **✔ A. `Ownable`'s constructor takes the first owner, so `contract C is Ownable { constructor() {} }` does not compile**
- **✔ B. `SafeERC20.safeTransfer` works with tokens that return nothing, and reverts with `SafeERC20FailedOperation(token)` when a token returns `false`**
- **✔ C. A token that inherits both `ERC20Capped` and `ERC20Pausable` must override `_update` and call `super._update`**
- D. `ReentrancyGuardTransient` keeps its lock in an ordinary storage slot, so it works on any EVM version

> **Why:** 5.0 made the first owner a constructor argument; without it solc says `No arguments passed to
> the base constructor. Specify the arguments or mark "C" as abstract.` `SafeERC20` accepts an
> empty return value (old tokens) and treats an explicit `false` as failure. Both extensions
> override `_update`, so solc demands `override(ERC20Capped, ERC20Pausable)` (error 6480), and
> `super._update` runs both. `ReentrancyGuardTransient` uses transient storage (`tstore`,
> EIP-1153), so it needs a chain with the Cancun upgrade or later; the storage-based
> `ReentrancyGuard` is marked deprecated in 5.7's source.

**Question 23** · One answer · `sol-medium-23`

A Foundry script deploys inside `vm.startBroadcast()` with a salt:

```solidity
registry = new Registry{salt: SALT}(admin);
```

and `Registry`'s constructor stores `msg.sender` as `deployer`. Who is `deployer` after the
script runs?

- **✔ A. The CREATE2 factory at `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C`, because forge sends salted deployments through it when broadcasting**
- B. The account that signs the broadcast, given with `--account` or `--sender`
- C. The script contract itself, because it executes `new`
- D. `admin`, because it is the constructor argument

> **Why:** Under a broadcast, forge turns `new X{salt: s}(...)` into a call to the deterministic CREATE2
> factory, which runs CREATE2. The factory is therefore the creator, both in the address
> formula and as `msg.sender` in the constructor: the real run logged `salted deployer:
> 0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C`. Without a salt the broadcaster deploys and is
> `msg.sender`. Never set an owner from `msg.sender` in a contract you deploy with a salt: pass
> the owner as an argument.

**Question 24** · One answer · `sol-medium-24`

`DeployLanterns` deploys `new LanternTickets{salt: SALT}(organiser, price)` inside a broadcast,
so it goes through forge's CREATE2 factory. Which change gives the tickets contract a
**different** address?

- **✔ A. Running it with `PRICE=20000000000000000` instead of the default 0.01 ether**
- B. Signing with another account, `--sender 0x...0B0B` instead of `--sender 0x...A11CE`
- C. Running it on another chain that has the same factory
- D. Running it a week later, at a higher block number

> **Why:** The CREATE2 address is `keccak256(0xff ++ creator ++ salt ++ keccak256(initCode))`, and the
> init code is the creation code followed by the encoded constructor arguments. A new price
> changes the init code: the simulation printed `0x13ADb8D0...a336` instead of
> `0xC5A06Cb1...7cE7`. The creator is the factory, not the signer, so two different
> `--sender` values gave the same `0xC5A06Cb1...7cE7`, and neither the chain nor the time
> appears in the formula. That is what makes CREATE2 addresses the same on every chain, as
> long as the compiler settings are identical.

#### Lab: Quayside Fish Auction

*Solidity · about 60 minutes · 10 s per test.* Build a fish auction paid in an OpenZeppelin ERC-20, with a basis-points value type and library for fees, Ownable2Step and a transient reentrancy guard, deadlines that a late bid extends, and pull payments for refunds, proceeds and fees, tested with pranks, warps, expected reverts and events, fuzzing and a token that calls back.

**Scenario**

Every morning at Kittiwake Quay the boats come in at dawn and the catch is sold on the quayside
before the cafés open. For years the harbour master ran the auction with a clipboard and a cash
tin: bids shouted across the fish boxes, a buyer outbid at the last second arguing that the
bell had already rung, and the harbour's fee worked out in pencil at the end of the week. The
harbour now issues its own token, Harbour Credit, which the boats and the buyers already use for
mooring fees and ice, and the harbour master wants the auction itself on chain: a boat lists a
box with a reserve price and a closing time, buyers bid in Harbour Credit, a late bid gives
everyone else five more minutes, and when the auction closes the boat gets its money less the
harbour's small fee. Nobody's credit may ever be stuck, nobody may be paid twice, and the fee
promised when a box was listed is the fee that is charged.

**Instructions**

Write `solution.sol`. The starter declares the value type, the library, both contracts, their
state, events and errors, the `Auction` struct and two helpers, `auctionOf` and `_existing`.
Keep every name and signature; write the bodies and add the modifiers the rules need. Use
OpenZeppelin 5.7 (already imported) for ownership, the reentrancy guard and token transfers.

**The value type.** `Bps` is a `uint16` of basis points: 250 is 2.5%. `using BpsMath for Bps
global` lets you write `fee.applyTo(amount)` anywhere.

1. **`BpsMath.applyTo(Bps share, uint256 amount)`**: `amount * share / 10_000`, rounded down
   (multiply first). 2.5% of 120 HBC is 3 HBC; 0.01% of 9,999 wei is 0.
2. **`HarbourCredit.mint(address to, uint256 amount)`**: only the owner, the harbour master
   (`onlyOwner`); mints with `_mint`. A stranger gets `OwnableUnauthorizedAccount(stranger)`.
3. **SafeERC20.** In `FishAuction`, attach `SafeERC20` to `IERC20`; move tokens only with
   `credit.safeTransferFrom` and `credit.safeTransfer`.
4. **Fees.** `_setFee(newFee)` reverts with `FeeTooHigh(newFee)` above `MAX_FEE` (1,000 bps),
   emits `FeeChanged(oldFee, newFee)` and stores it; the constructor already calls it.
   `setFee(newFee)` is `onlyOwner` and calls `_setFee`. A fee change affects only catches
   listed afterwards.
5. **`list(uint256 reserve, uint256 duration) returns (uint256 id)`**: anyone may list. Revert
   with `ZeroDuration()` for a duration of 0. Ids count up from 1 (`auctionCount` is the last
   id). Store an `Auction` with `msg.sender` as seller, `endsAt = block.timestamp + duration`,
   **the current `fee`**, and the reserve; emit `Listed(id, seller, reserve, endsAt)`.
6. **`minimumBid(uint256 id)`**: `UnknownAuction(id)` through `_existing`. With no bid yet, the
   reserve, or 1 when the reserve is 0. Otherwise the highest bid plus
   `MIN_RAISE.applyTo(highestBid)`, or plus 1 when that raise rounds down to 0.
7. **`bid(uint256 id, uint256 amount)`**, `nonReentrant`, checks in this order:
   - the auction exists (`UnknownAuction(id)`);
   - `block.timestamp < endsAt`, otherwise `AuctionEnded(id)`;
   - the caller is not the seller (`SellerCannotBid()`);
   - `amount >= minimumBid(id)`, otherwise `BidTooLow(id, minimum)`.

   Then, before any token moves: credit the previous highest bid, if any, to its bidder in
   `withdrawable` (never send it back directly); record the new highest bidder and bid; if
   **less than** `EXTENSION` (5 minutes) is left (`endsAt - block.timestamp < EXTENSION`), set
   `endsAt = block.timestamp + EXTENSION`; emit `BidPlaced(id, bidder, amount, endsAt)` with the
   end as it now is. Last, pull the bid: `credit.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount)`.
8. **`settle(uint256 id)`**: anyone; `UnknownAuction(id)`; before `endsAt` revert with
   `AuctionNotEnded(id, endsAt)`; a second time revert with `AlreadySettled(id)`. Mark it
   settled. With a winner, the fee is the auction's own `fee` applied to the highest bid: credit
   the seller the bid minus the fee and the **current owner** (`owner()`) the fee. Emit
   `Settled(id, winner, price, fee)`, which is `Settled(id, address(0), 0, 0)` when nobody bid.
9. **`withdraw()`**, `nonReentrant`: revert with `NothingToWithdraw()` when nothing is credited;
   otherwise zero the credit, emit `Withdrawn(account, amount)` and `safeTransfer` the amount.

The tests also use a token whose transfers call back into the auction: both `bid` and
`withdraw` must then revert with OpenZeppelin's `ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall()`.

**The morning at the quayside** (the visible test). The fee is 250 bps. At timestamp 1,000,000
the skipper lists a box with a reserve of 100 HBC for one hour, so it ends at 1,003,600:

| Time | Event | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1,000,000 | Ada bids 100 HBC | `BidPlaced(1, ada, 100e18, 1003600)` |
| | Ben bids 104 HBC | `BidTooLow(1, 105e18)`: 5% more is needed |
| | Ben bids 105 HBC | Ada is credited 100 HBC |
| 1,003,540 | Ada bids 120 HBC, one minute before the end | the end moves to 1,003,840; Ben is credited 105 HBC |
| 1,003,600 | `settle(1)` | `AuctionNotEnded(1, 1003840)` |
| 1,003,840 | `settle(1)` | `Settled(1, ada, 120e18, 3e18)`: the skipper is credited 117 HBC, the harbour master 3 HBC |

After everyone withdraws, Ada has 880 HBC of her 1,000, Ben his 1,000, the skipper 117 and the
harbour master 3, and the auction holds nothing.

**Boilerplate given to the learner** (`starter.sol`)

```solidity
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity ^0.8.24;

import {Ownable, Ownable2Step} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable2Step.sol";
import {ERC20} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol";
import {IERC20} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol";
import {SafeERC20} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol";
import {ReentrancyGuardTransient} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuardTransient.sol";

/// @notice A share in basis points: 1 bps is 0.01%, 10_000 bps is 100%.
type Bps is uint16;

/// @notice Fee arithmetic on Bps.
library BpsMath {
    uint256 internal constant DENOMINATOR = 10_000;

    /// @notice `share` of `amount`, rounded down. (Task 1)
    function applyTo(Bps share, uint256 amount) internal pure returns (uint256) {
        revert("not implemented: applyTo");
    }
}

using BpsMath for Bps global;

/// @notice The harbour's own token, Harbour Credit (HBC). The harbour master mints it.
contract HarbourCredit is ERC20, Ownable {
    constructor(address harbourMaster) ERC20("Harbour Credit", "HBC") Ownable(harbourMaster) {}

    /// @notice Mint `amount` HBC to `to`. Only the harbour master. (Task 2)
    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {
        revert("not implemented: mint");
    }
}

/// @notice The quayside auction: boats list a catch, buyers bid in Harbour Credit until the
/// deadline, and a late bid extends it. Every payment is credited and then withdrawn.
contract FishAuction is Ownable2Step, ReentrancyGuardTransient {
    // Task 3: attach SafeERC20 to IERC20.

    /// @notice A bid with less than this left extends the auction to this much from now.
    uint256 public constant EXTENSION = 5 minutes;
    /// @notice Each bid must beat the last one by at least this share (and by at least 1).
    Bps public constant MIN_RAISE = Bps.wrap(500);
    /// @notice The highest fee the harbour master may set.
    Bps public constant MAX_FEE = Bps.wrap(1_000);

    struct Auction {
        address seller;
        uint64 endsAt;
        Bps fee; // the harbour's fee, fixed when the catch is listed
        bool settled;
        address highestBidder;
        uint256 highestBid;
        uint256 reserve;
    }

    IERC20 public immutable credit;
    Bps public fee;
    uint256 public auctionCount;
    mapping(uint256 id => Auction) internal auctions;
    mapping(address account => uint256) public withdrawable;

    event FeeChanged(Bps oldFee, Bps newFee);
    event Listed(uint256 indexed id, address indexed seller, uint256 reserve, uint256 endsAt);
    event BidPlaced(uint256 indexed id, address indexed bidder, uint256 amount, uint256 endsAt);
    event Settled(uint256 indexed id, address indexed winner, uint256 price, uint256 fee);
    event Withdrawn(address indexed account, uint256 amount);

    error FeeTooHigh(Bps fee);
    error ZeroDuration();
    error UnknownAuction(uint256 id);
    error SellerCannotBid();
    error BidTooLow(uint256 id, uint256 minimum);
    error AuctionEnded(uint256 id);
    error AuctionNotEnded(uint256 id, uint256 endsAt);
    error AlreadySettled(uint256 id);
    error NothingToWithdraw();

    constructor(IERC20 credit_, address harbourMaster, Bps fee_) Ownable(harbourMaster) {
        credit = credit_;
        _setFee(fee_);
    }

    /// @notice Change the fee for catches listed from now on. Only the harbour master. (Task 4)
    function setFee(Bps newFee) external {
        revert("not implemented: setFee");
    }

    /// @notice List a catch with a reserve price, for `duration` seconds. Ids start at 1. (Task 5)
    function list(uint256 reserve, uint256 duration) external returns (uint256 id) {
        revert("not implemented: list");
    }

    /// @notice The lowest bid auction `id` accepts now. (Task 6)
    function minimumBid(uint256 id) public view returns (uint256) {
        revert("not implemented: minimumBid");
    }

    /// @notice Bid `amount` HBC; the auction must be approved for it. (Task 7)
    function bid(uint256 id, uint256 amount) external {
        revert("not implemented: bid");
    }

    /// @notice After the deadline, anyone may settle. (Task 8)
    function settle(uint256 id) external {
        revert("not implemented: settle");
    }

    /// @notice Withdraw everything credited to you. (Task 9)
    function withdraw() external {
        revert("not implemented: withdraw");
    }

    function auctionOf(uint256 id) external view returns (Auction memory) {
        return _existing(id);
    }

    /// @dev The auction `id`, or UnknownAuction(id) if there is none.
    function _existing(uint256 id) internal view returns (Auction storage a) {
        if (id == 0 || id > auctionCount) revert UnknownAuction(id);
        a = auctions[id];
    }

    /// @dev Checks and stores a new fee. (Task 4)
    function _setFee(Bps newFee) internal {
        revert("not implemented: _setFee");
    }
}
```

**Test cases the backend runs**

**Test 1: Works through the morning at the quayside from the instructions** (visible)

```solidity
/// The morning from the instructions, step by step.
contract QuaysideMorningTest is Test {
    event Listed(uint256 indexed id, address indexed seller, uint256 reserve, uint256 endsAt);
    event BidPlaced(uint256 indexed id, address indexed bidder, uint256 amount, uint256 endsAt);
    event Settled(uint256 indexed id, address indexed winner, uint256 price, uint256 fee);

    function test_a_morning_at_the_quayside() public {
        address master = makeAddr("harbour master");
        address skipper = makeAddr("skipper");
        address ada = makeAddr("ada");
        address ben = makeAddr("ben");

        HarbourCredit credit = new HarbourCredit(master);
        FishAuction auction = new FishAuction(credit, master, Bps.wrap(250));
        vm.startPrank(master);
        credit.mint(ada, 1_000e18);
        credit.mint(ben, 1_000e18);
        vm.stopPrank();
        vm.prank(ada);
        credit.approve(address(auction), type(uint256).max);
        vm.prank(ben);
        credit.approve(address(auction), type(uint256).max);

        // 06:00: the skipper lists a box of mackerel, reserve 100 HBC, for one hour.
        vm.warp(1_000_000);
        uint256 end = 1_000_000 + 1 hours;
        vm.expectEmit(address(auction));
        emit Listed(1, skipper, 100e18, end);
        vm.prank(skipper);
        uint256 id = auction.list(100e18, 1 hours);
        assertEq(id, 1, "the first auction's id");

        vm.expectEmit(address(auction));
        emit BidPlaced(id, ada, 100e18, end);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, 100e18);

        // A raise of less than 5% is refused, with the minimum in the error.
        vm.prank(ben);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.BidTooLow.selector, id, 105e18));
        auction.bid(id, 104e18);
        vm.prank(ben);
        auction.bid(id, 105e18);
        assertEq(auction.withdrawable(ada), 100e18, "ada's outbid 100 HBC, credited back to her");

        // One minute before the end, ada bids again: the end moves to five minutes from now.
        vm.warp(end - 1 minutes);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, 120e18);
        uint256 newEnd = end - 1 minutes + 5 minutes;
        assertEq(auction.auctionOf(id).endsAt, newEnd, "the end after a late bid");

        vm.warp(end);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.AuctionNotEnded.selector, id, newEnd));
        auction.settle(id);

        vm.warp(newEnd);
        vm.expectEmit(address(auction));
        emit Settled(id, ada, 120e18, 3e18);
        auction.settle(id);
        assertEq(auction.withdrawable(skipper), 117e18, "the skipper's proceeds after the 2.5% fee");
        assertEq(auction.withdrawable(master), 3e18, "the harbour's fee");

        address[4] memory everyone = [ada, ben, skipper, master];
        for (uint256 i = 0; i < everyone.length; i++) {
            vm.prank(everyone[i]);
            auction.withdraw();
        }
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(ada), 880e18, "ada's HBC after buying for 120");
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(ben), 1_000e18, "ben's HBC after being outbid");
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(skipper), 117e18, "the skipper's HBC");
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(master), 3e18, "the harbour master's HBC");
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(address(auction)), 0, "the HBC left in the auction");
    }
}
```

**Test 2: Mints Harbour Credit and charges the right fee to the right account** (hidden)

```solidity
import {Ownable} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable.sol";

/// Exposes the library to the test: BpsMath's functions are internal.
contract BpsProbe {
    function applyTo(Bps share, uint256 amount) external pure returns (uint256) {
        return share.applyTo(amount);
    }
}

contract CreditAndFeesTest is Test {
    event FeeChanged(Bps oldFee, Bps newFee);

    address master = makeAddr("harbour master");
    address stranger = makeAddr("stranger");
    HarbourCredit credit;

    function setUp() public {
        credit = new HarbourCredit(master);
    }

    function test_the_credit_token() public {
        assertEq(credit.name(), "Harbour Credit", "the token's name");
        assertEq(credit.symbol(), "HBC", "the token's symbol");
        assertEq(credit.decimals(), 18, "the token's decimals");
        assertEq(credit.owner(), master, "the token's owner");
        vm.prank(master);
        credit.mint(stranger, 5e18);
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(stranger), 5e18, "a balance after minting");
        assertEq(credit.totalSupply(), 5e18, "the supply after minting");
    }

    function test_only_the_harbour_master_mints() public {
        vm.prank(stranger);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(Ownable.OwnableUnauthorizedAccount.selector, stranger));
        credit.mint(stranger, 1);
    }

    function testFuzz_a_share_of_an_amount(uint16 bps, uint256 amount) public {
        bps = uint16(bound(bps, 0, 10_000));
        amount = bound(amount, 0, 1e30);
        BpsProbe probe = new BpsProbe();
        assertEq(probe.applyTo(Bps.wrap(bps), amount), amount * bps / 10_000, "a share in basis points");
    }

    function test_shares_round_down() public {
        BpsProbe probe = new BpsProbe();
        assertEq(probe.applyTo(Bps.wrap(250), 120e18), 3e18, "2.5% of 120 HBC");
        assertEq(probe.applyTo(Bps.wrap(1), 9_999), 0, "0.01% of 9999 wei");
        assertEq(probe.applyTo(Bps.wrap(10_000), 7), 7, "100% of 7 wei");
    }

    function test_the_constructor_refuses_a_fee_above_the_maximum() public {
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.FeeTooHigh.selector, Bps.wrap(1_001)));
        new FishAuction(credit, master, Bps.wrap(1_001));
    }

    function test_the_harbour_master_sets_the_fee() public {
        FishAuction auction = new FishAuction(credit, master, Bps.wrap(250));
        assertEq(Bps.unwrap(auction.fee()), 250, "the fee from the constructor");

        vm.prank(stranger);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(Ownable.OwnableUnauthorizedAccount.selector, stranger));
        auction.setFee(Bps.wrap(100));

        vm.expectEmit(address(auction));
        emit FeeChanged(Bps.wrap(250), Bps.wrap(1_000));
        vm.prank(master);
        auction.setFee(Bps.wrap(1_000));
        assertEq(Bps.unwrap(auction.fee()), 1_000, "the fee after setFee");

        vm.prank(master);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.FeeTooHigh.selector, Bps.wrap(1_001)));
        auction.setFee(Bps.wrap(1_001));
    }

    function test_the_fee_is_fixed_when_the_catch_is_listed() public {
        FishAuction auction = new FishAuction(credit, master, Bps.wrap(250));
        address skipper = makeAddr("skipper");
        address buyer = makeAddr("buyer");
        vm.prank(master);
        credit.mint(buyer, 1_000e18);
        vm.prank(buyer);
        credit.approve(address(auction), type(uint256).max);

        vm.prank(skipper);
        uint256 id = auction.list(10e18, 1 hours);
        assertEq(Bps.unwrap(auction.auctionOf(id).fee), 250, "the fee recorded with the auction");
        vm.prank(buyer);
        auction.bid(id, 200e18);
        vm.prank(master);
        auction.setFee(Bps.wrap(1_000));

        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 hours);
        auction.settle(id);
        assertEq(auction.withdrawable(master), 5e18, "the fee charged after the fee was raised");
        assertEq(auction.withdrawable(skipper), 195e18, "the skipper's proceeds after the fee was raised");
    }

    function test_the_fee_goes_to_the_current_harbour_master() public {
        FishAuction auction = new FishAuction(credit, master, Bps.wrap(500));
        address nextMaster = makeAddr("next harbour master");
        address buyer = makeAddr("buyer");
        vm.prank(master);
        credit.mint(buyer, 100e18);
        vm.prank(buyer);
        credit.approve(address(auction), type(uint256).max);
        uint256 id = auction.list(1e18, 1 hours);
        vm.prank(buyer);
        auction.bid(id, 40e18);

        vm.prank(master);
        auction.transferOwnership(nextMaster);
        assertEq(auction.owner(), master, "the owner before the handover is accepted");
        vm.prank(nextMaster);
        auction.acceptOwnership();

        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 hours);
        auction.settle(id);
        assertEq(auction.withdrawable(nextMaster), 2e18, "the fee credited to the new harbour master");
        assertEq(auction.withdrawable(master), 0, "the fee credited to the old harbour master");
    }
}
```

**Test 3: Enforces the bidding rules and credits every outbid bid** (hidden)

```solidity
import {IERC20Errors} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/interfaces/draft-IERC6093.sol";

contract BiddingRulesTest is Test {
    event BidPlaced(uint256 indexed id, address indexed bidder, uint256 amount, uint256 endsAt);

    address master = makeAddr("harbour master");
    address skipper = makeAddr("skipper");
    address ada = makeAddr("ada");
    address ben = makeAddr("ben");
    HarbourCredit credit;
    FishAuction auction;
    uint256 id;

    function setUp() public {
        credit = new HarbourCredit(master);
        auction = new FishAuction(credit, master, Bps.wrap(300));
        address[3] memory buyers = [ada, ben, skipper];
        for (uint256 i = 0; i < buyers.length; i++) {
            vm.prank(master);
            credit.mint(buyers[i], 10_000e18);
            vm.prank(buyers[i]);
            credit.approve(address(auction), type(uint256).max);
        }
        vm.prank(skipper);
        id = auction.list(50e18, 2 hours);
    }

    function test_unknown_auctions_are_refused() public {
        vm.prank(ada);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.UnknownAuction.selector, 0));
        auction.bid(0, 60e18);
        vm.prank(ada);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.UnknownAuction.selector, 2));
        auction.bid(2, 60e18);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.UnknownAuction.selector, 2));
        auction.minimumBid(2);
    }

    function test_the_seller_cannot_bid_on_their_own_catch() public {
        vm.prank(skipper);
        vm.expectRevert(FishAuction.SellerCannotBid.selector);
        auction.bid(id, 60e18);
    }

    function test_the_first_bid_must_meet_the_reserve() public {
        assertEq(auction.minimumBid(id), 50e18, "the minimum before any bid");
        vm.prank(ada);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.BidTooLow.selector, id, 50e18));
        auction.bid(id, 50e18 - 1);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, 50e18);
    }

    function test_a_catch_without_reserve_still_needs_a_bid_above_zero() public {
        vm.prank(skipper);
        uint256 free = auction.list(0, 1 hours);
        assertEq(auction.minimumBid(free), 1, "the minimum with no reserve");
        vm.prank(ada);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.BidTooLow.selector, free, 1));
        auction.bid(free, 0);
    }

    function test_each_bid_must_beat_the_last_by_five_percent() public {
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, 80e18);
        assertEq(auction.minimumBid(id), 84e18, "the minimum after a bid of 80 HBC");
        vm.prank(ben);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.BidTooLow.selector, id, 84e18));
        auction.bid(id, 84e18 - 1);
        vm.prank(ben);
        auction.bid(id, 84e18);
    }

    function test_a_tiny_bid_must_still_be_beaten_by_one() public {
        vm.prank(skipper);
        uint256 cheap = auction.list(10, 1 hours);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(cheap, 10);
        assertEq(auction.minimumBid(cheap), 11, "the minimum after a bid of 10 wei");
        vm.prank(ben);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.BidTooLow.selector, cheap, 11));
        auction.bid(cheap, 10);
    }

    function test_an_outbid_bid_is_credited_not_sent() public {
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, 100e18);
        vm.prank(ben);
        auction.bid(id, 200e18);
        assertEq(auction.withdrawable(ada), 100e18, "ada's credit after being outbid");
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(ada), 9_900e18, "ada's wallet after being outbid, before withdrawing");
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(address(auction)), 300e18, "the HBC the auction holds");

        FishAuction.Auction memory a = auction.auctionOf(id);
        assertEq(a.highestBidder, ben, "the highest bidder");
        assertEq(a.highestBid, 200e18, "the highest bid");
    }

    function test_a_bid_is_announced() public {
        uint256 endsAt = auction.auctionOf(id).endsAt;
        vm.expectEmit(address(auction));
        emit BidPlaced(id, ada, 75e18, endsAt);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, 75e18);
    }

    function test_a_bid_needs_an_allowance() public {
        address carl = makeAddr("carl");
        vm.prank(master);
        credit.mint(carl, 100e18);
        vm.prank(carl);
        vm.expectRevert(
            abi.encodeWithSelector(IERC20Errors.ERC20InsufficientAllowance.selector, address(auction), 0, 60e18)
        );
        auction.bid(id, 60e18);
    }

    function testFuzz_the_auction_holds_every_live_bid(uint256 first, uint256 second, uint256 third) public {
        first = bound(first, 50e18, 1_000e18);
        second = bound(second, first + first * 500 / 10_000, 2_000e18);
        third = bound(third, second + second * 500 / 10_000, 4_000e18);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, first);
        vm.prank(ben);
        auction.bid(id, second);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, third);
        assertEq(auction.withdrawable(ada), first, "ada's credit");
        assertEq(auction.withdrawable(ben), second, "ben's credit");
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(address(auction)), first + second + third, "the HBC the auction holds");
    }
}
```

**Test 4: Keeps the deadlines, the extension and settlement exactly** (hidden)

```solidity
contract DeadlinesTest is Test {
    event Listed(uint256 indexed id, address indexed seller, uint256 reserve, uint256 endsAt);
    event Settled(uint256 indexed id, address indexed winner, uint256 price, uint256 fee);

    address master = makeAddr("harbour master");
    address skipper = makeAddr("skipper");
    address ada = makeAddr("ada");
    address ben = makeAddr("ben");
    HarbourCredit credit;
    FishAuction auction;
    uint256 constant START = 2_000_000;

    function setUp() public {
        vm.warp(START);
        credit = new HarbourCredit(master);
        auction = new FishAuction(credit, master, Bps.wrap(100));
        address[2] memory buyers = [ada, ben];
        for (uint256 i = 0; i < buyers.length; i++) {
            vm.prank(master);
            credit.mint(buyers[i], 10_000e18);
            vm.prank(buyers[i]);
            credit.approve(address(auction), type(uint256).max);
        }
    }

    function _list(uint256 duration) internal returns (uint256) {
        vm.prank(skipper);
        return auction.list(1e18, duration);
    }

    function test_listing_numbers_and_announces_each_catch() public {
        vm.expectEmit(address(auction));
        emit Listed(1, skipper, 1e18, START + 30 minutes);
        assertEq(_list(30 minutes), 1, "the first id");
        assertEq(_list(1 hours), 2, "the second id");
        assertEq(auction.auctionCount(), 2, "the number of auctions");
        FishAuction.Auction memory a = auction.auctionOf(2);
        assertEq(a.seller, skipper, "the seller");
        assertEq(a.endsAt, START + 1 hours, "the end of the second auction");
        assertEq(a.reserve, 1e18, "the reserve");
    }

    function test_a_listing_needs_a_duration() public {
        vm.prank(skipper);
        vm.expectRevert(FishAuction.ZeroDuration.selector);
        auction.list(1e18, 0);
    }

    function test_bids_are_taken_until_the_second_before_the_end() public {
        uint256 id = _list(1 hours);
        vm.warp(START + 1 hours - 1);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, 2e18);
        uint256 endsAt = auction.auctionOf(id).endsAt;
        vm.warp(endsAt);
        vm.prank(ben);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.AuctionEnded.selector, id));
        auction.bid(id, 5e18);
    }

    function test_a_bid_with_exactly_five_minutes_left_does_not_extend() public {
        uint256 id = _list(1 hours);
        vm.warp(START + 1 hours - 5 minutes);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, 2e18);
        assertEq(auction.auctionOf(id).endsAt, START + 1 hours, "the end after a bid with five minutes left");
    }

    function test_a_bid_with_less_than_five_minutes_left_extends() public {
        uint256 id = _list(1 hours);
        uint256 bidAt = START + 1 hours - 5 minutes + 1;
        vm.warp(bidAt);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, 2e18);
        assertEq(auction.auctionOf(id).endsAt, bidAt + 5 minutes, "the end after a bid with 4:59 left");
    }

    function testFuzz_a_bid_leaves_at_least_five_minutes(uint256 bidAt) public {
        uint256 id = _list(1 hours);
        bidAt = bound(bidAt, START, START + 1 hours - 1);
        vm.warp(bidAt);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, 2e18);
        uint256 expected = START + 1 hours;
        if (expected - bidAt < 5 minutes) expected = bidAt + 5 minutes;
        assertEq(auction.auctionOf(id).endsAt, expected, "the end after a bid");
    }

    function test_settling_waits_for_the_end() public {
        uint256 id = _list(1 hours);
        vm.warp(START + 1 hours - 1);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.AuctionNotEnded.selector, id, START + 1 hours));
        auction.settle(id);
        vm.warp(START + 1 hours);
        auction.settle(id);
        assertTrue(auction.auctionOf(id).settled, "whether the auction is settled");
    }

    function test_an_auction_settles_only_once() public {
        uint256 id = _list(1 hours);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, 10e18);
        vm.warp(START + 1 hours);
        auction.settle(id);
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.AlreadySettled.selector, id));
        auction.settle(id);
        assertEq(auction.withdrawable(skipper), 9.9e18, "the proceeds after settling twice");
    }

    function test_a_catch_nobody_bid_on_settles_with_nothing_paid() public {
        uint256 id = _list(1 hours);
        vm.warp(START + 2 hours);
        vm.expectEmit(address(auction));
        emit Settled(id, address(0), 0, 0);
        auction.settle(id);
        assertEq(auction.withdrawable(skipper), 0, "the proceeds of an unsold catch");
        assertEq(auction.withdrawable(master), 0, "the fee on an unsold catch");
    }

    function test_unknown_auctions_cannot_be_settled() public {
        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(FishAuction.UnknownAuction.selector, 7));
        auction.settle(7);
    }
}
```

**Test 5: Pays every credit once and refuses a token that calls back** (hidden)

```solidity
import {ReentrancyGuardTransient} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuardTransient.sol";

/// A token with a transfer hook that calls back into the auction while it moves tokens.
contract HookedCredit {
    mapping(address => uint256) public balanceOf;
    FishAuction public target;
    bytes public callback;

    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {
        balanceOf[to] += amount;
    }

    function arm(FishAuction target_, bytes calldata callback_) external {
        target = target_;
        callback = callback_;
    }

    function transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 amount) external returns (bool) {
        balanceOf[from] -= amount;
        balanceOf[to] += amount;
        _hook();
        return true;
    }

    function transfer(address to, uint256 amount) external returns (bool) {
        balanceOf[msg.sender] -= amount;
        balanceOf[to] += amount;
        _hook();
        return true;
    }

    function _hook() internal {
        if (callback.length == 0) return;
        bytes memory data = callback;
        delete callback;
        (bool ok, bytes memory reason) = address(target).call(data);
        if (!ok) {
            assembly {
                revert(add(reason, 32), mload(reason))
            }
        }
    }
}

contract WithdrawalsTest is Test {
    event Withdrawn(address indexed account, uint256 amount);

    address master = makeAddr("harbour master");
    address skipper = makeAddr("skipper");
    address ada = makeAddr("ada");
    address ben = makeAddr("ben");
    address cy = makeAddr("cy");

    function _market() internal returns (HarbourCredit credit, FishAuction auction) {
        credit = new HarbourCredit(master);
        auction = new FishAuction(credit, master, Bps.wrap(250));
        address[3] memory buyers = [ada, ben, cy];
        for (uint256 i = 0; i < buyers.length; i++) {
            vm.prank(master);
            credit.mint(buyers[i], 10_000e18);
            vm.prank(buyers[i]);
            credit.approve(address(auction), type(uint256).max);
        }
    }

    function test_nothing_to_withdraw() public {
        (, FishAuction auction) = _market();
        vm.prank(ada);
        vm.expectRevert(FishAuction.NothingToWithdraw.selector);
        auction.withdraw();
    }

    function test_a_withdrawal_pays_once_and_is_announced() public {
        (HarbourCredit credit, FishAuction auction) = _market();
        vm.prank(skipper);
        uint256 id = auction.list(1e18, 1 hours);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, 10e18);
        vm.prank(ben);
        auction.bid(id, 20e18);

        vm.expectEmit(address(auction));
        emit Withdrawn(ada, 10e18);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.withdraw();
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(ada), 10_000e18, "ada's HBC after withdrawing her outbid bid");
        assertEq(auction.withdrawable(ada), 0, "ada's credit after withdrawing");
        vm.prank(ada);
        vm.expectRevert(FishAuction.NothingToWithdraw.selector);
        auction.withdraw();
    }

    function testFuzz_every_credit_is_paid_and_nothing_is_left(uint256 a, uint256 b, uint256 c, uint16 feeBps) public {
        (HarbourCredit credit, FishAuction auction) = _market();
        vm.prank(master);
        auction.setFee(Bps.wrap(uint16(bound(feeBps, 0, 1_000))));
        a = bound(a, 1, 1_000e18);
        b = bound(b, a + a * 500 / 10_000 + 1, 2_000e18);
        c = bound(c, b + b * 500 / 10_000 + 1, 4_000e18);

        vm.prank(skipper);
        uint256 id = auction.list(1, 1 hours);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, a);
        vm.prank(ben);
        auction.bid(id, b);
        vm.prank(cy);
        auction.bid(id, c);
        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 hours);
        auction.settle(id);

        address[5] memory everyone = [ada, ben, cy, skipper, master];
        for (uint256 i = 0; i < everyone.length; i++) {
            if (auction.withdrawable(everyone[i]) > 0) {
                vm.prank(everyone[i]);
                auction.withdraw();
            }
        }
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(address(auction)), 0, "the HBC left in the auction");
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(ada), 10_000e18, "ada's HBC after being outbid");
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(ben), 10_000e18, "ben's HBC after being outbid");
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(cy), 10_000e18 - c, "the winner's HBC");
        assertEq(credit.balanceOf(skipper) + credit.balanceOf(master), c, "the seller's and the harbour's HBC together");
    }

    function test_a_token_cannot_call_back_into_withdraw_during_a_bid() public {
        HookedCredit hooked = new HookedCredit();
        FishAuction auction = new FishAuction(IERC20(address(hooked)), master, Bps.wrap(250));
        hooked.mint(ada, 100e18);
        vm.prank(skipper);
        uint256 id = auction.list(1e18, 1 hours);
        hooked.arm(auction, abi.encodeCall(FishAuction.withdraw, ()));
        vm.prank(ada);
        vm.expectRevert(ReentrancyGuardTransient.ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.selector);
        auction.bid(id, 10e18);
    }

    function test_a_token_cannot_call_back_into_bid_during_a_withdrawal() public {
        HookedCredit hooked = new HookedCredit();
        FishAuction auction = new FishAuction(IERC20(address(hooked)), master, Bps.wrap(250));
        hooked.mint(ada, 100e18);
        hooked.mint(ben, 100e18);
        vm.prank(skipper);
        uint256 id = auction.list(1e18, 1 hours);
        vm.prank(ada);
        auction.bid(id, 10e18);
        vm.prank(ben);
        auction.bid(id, 20e18);
        hooked.arm(auction, abi.encodeCall(FishAuction.bid, (id, 50e18)));
        vm.prank(ada);
        vm.expectRevert(ReentrancyGuardTransient.ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.selector);
        auction.withdraw();
    }
}
```
